newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada warns against giving in to Peru gunmen.
newsitem.headline: Canada warns against giving in to Peru gunmen.

text.p: Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Wednesday up to 490 diplomats and others being held hostage by armed guerrillas in Peru were being treated well by their captors, but he warned that giving in to the guerrillas' demands would worsen the situation.

"Reports that we've had is that so far they (the hostages) have been given proper treatment," Axworthy told reporters. "We are clearly calling for moderation declared for those who are holding them captive," he said.

"But at the same time, they've issued various demands that the Peruvian government release a number of their cohorts. I think a pretty fundamental principle is that to give in to those kinds of demands simply exacerbates and increases the problem."

Axworthy said Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien would call Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori to offer Canada's assistance in resolving the hostage crisis. Four Canadians are among the hostages being held at the residence of the Japanese ambassador in Lima.

They include Canada's ambassador to Peru, Anthony Vincent, an aid worker and two businessmen. Three Canadian women including the ambassador's wife and the wife of one of the businessmen have been released, a foreign affairs spokeswoman said in Ottawa.

The hostages were taken by the leftist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) on Tuesday night. The gunmen have threatened to kill them unless the Peruvian government frees 400 to 500 jailed MRTA guerrillas.

Awxorthy said the Peruvian government had established a negotiating team but it was not clear what kind of contact the team had had with the rebels. "The primary negotiations are taking place by the Peruvian officials. We have confidence in their ability to do that and we simply want to support these efforts," he said.
